note.explanation: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure by the height of a mercury column. Air pressure supports the mercury, and changes in atmospheric pressure can help forecast weather.
examples: At sea level, the textbook gives a mercury column height of 760 mm.
If water replaced mercury in a barometer, the column would need to be about 10.3 m high.
note.checkAnswer: Atmospheric pressure supports the mercury column; pressure at the same level in the mercury is equal.
note.simple: Air presses on the mercury in the dish and holds up a column of mercury in the barometer tube. A higher column means greater atmospheric pressure.
note.title: Measuring Atmospheric Pressure
steps: Fill a glass tube, closed at one end, completely with mercury.
Invert the tube vertically in a dish of mercury.
Measure the height of the mercury column with a scale.
Use the column height to find the atmospheric pressure.
note.answer: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure using the height of a mercury column.

options: The height of the mercury column it can support
The mass of air in a room
The area of the mercury surface in the dish
mcqs.stem: In a simple mercury barometer, atmospheric pressure is measured by the:
rationales: This is correct because atmospheric pressure is expressed by the height of the mercury column it supports.
This is incorrect because the barometer measures pressure, not the total mass of air in a room.
This is incorrect because the dish surface area is not used to determine the pressure.
This is incorrect because mercury temperature is not the barometer reading described in this section.

options: The pressure at A is greater than at B
The pressure at A is less than at B
The pressure at A equals the pressure at B
mcqs.stem: In the barometer, points A and B are at the same level in the mercury. How do their pressures compare?
rationales: This is incorrect because points at the same level in the same liquid have equal pressure.
This is incorrect because equal-level points in the same liquid do not have different pressures.
This is correct because pressure is the same at points A and B, which are at the same level in the mercury.
This is incorrect because their pressures can be compared using the same-level rule for a liquid.

mcqs.stem: What is ideally present in the space above the mercury in a simple barometer tube?
rationales: This is correct because the textbook describes the space above the mercury as completely empty, with pressure almost zero.
This is incorrect because air above the column would exert pressure and affect the reading.
This is incorrect because the space is described as empty, not filled with mercury vapour.
This is incorrect because the space above the mercury is not a solid stopper.

mcqs.stem: What is the height of the mercury column at sea level given in this section?
rationales: This is correct because the section states that the column height at sea level is 760 mm.
This is incorrect because 76 mm is one tenth of the stated column height.
This is incorrect because 7.6 mm is far below the stated column height.
This is incorrect because the stated height is 760 mm, or 0.760 m, not 7.6 m.

options: A change only in mercury density
mcqs.stem: According to this section, what may a fall in atmospheric pressure indicate?
rationales: This is correct because a fall in pressure often means rain clouds are on the way.
This is incorrect because the section connects falling, not rising, pressure with approaching rain clouds.
This is incorrect because the pressure is described as fluctuating and a fall has a weather indication.
This is incorrect because the section links pressure changes to weather and air density, not only mercury density.

options: The density of air is lower
The density of air is higher
mcqs.stem: Why does atmospheric pressure fall at high altitudes, according to the section?
rationales: This is correct because air is less dense at high altitudes, so atmospheric pressure falls.
This is incorrect because the section says air is less dense, not denser, at high altitudes.
This is incorrect because the explanation concerns air density, not a change in mercury density.
This is incorrect because the section does not say gravity becomes zero at high altitude.

mcqs.stem: Approximately how tall would a water column need to be to balance atmospheric pressure at sea level?
rationales: This is correct because water is much less dense than mercury, so the section's barometer calculation gives about 10.3 m.
This is incorrect because 0.76 m is the approximate height of mercury, not water.
This is incorrect because a 1.0 m water column would not balance sea-level atmospheric pressure.
This is incorrect because 13.6 m is not the result of the section's water-barometer calculation.

options: It can indicate changes that help forecast weather
It directly measures the amount of rain in a cloud
It measures the temperature of the atmosphere
mcqs.stem: How can observing atmospheric pressure help meteorologists?
rationales: This is correct because meteorologists observe pressure variations to forecast weather conditions.
This is incorrect because a barometer measures pressure, not the amount of rain inside a cloud.
This is incorrect because atmospheric pressure measurement does not directly measure wind speed.
This is incorrect because a barometer measures pressure, not atmospheric temperature.

written.text: What is the basic principle to measure the atmospheric pressure by a simple mercury barometer?
written.finalAnswer: Atmospheric pressure is equal to the pressure of the mercury column, ρgh, and is measured by the height of that column.

examTips: This topic can appear as a short-answer question asking for the basic principle of a mercury barometer; earn marks by mentioning the mercury-column height and the pressure relation P = ρgh.
A constructed-response question may ask how trapped air or a leak affects the barometer; state what happens to pressure above the mercury, then describe the change in column height and reading.
A numerical question may ask for the height of a different liquid column. Write P = ρgh, substitute the atmospheric pressure and liquid density, then solve for h with units.
For questions about weather, connect falling pressure with less-dense air or increasing water vapour and the possibility of rain clouds.

explain.title: What a barometer measures
explain.body: “Atmospheric pressure is usually measured by the height of mercury column which it can support.” Instruments which measure the atmospheric pressure are called barometers.

explain.title: How the simple mercury barometer works
explain.body: A tube closed at one end is filled with mercury and inverted in a dish of mercury. The space above the mercury is completely empty, so its pressure is almost zero. A scale beside the tube measures the column height.

explain.title: Why the column represents atmospheric pressure
explain.body: Points A and B are at the same level in the mercury, so their pressures are equal. The pressure at the mercury surface in the dish is atmospheric pressure, and the liquid-column pressure is P = ρgh.

explain.title: Pressure and weather
explain.body: Atmospheric pressure changes with conditions. At high altitudes air is less dense and pressure falls. More water vapour also lowers air density, so low pressure in cloudy regions can warn that rain may follow.

mistakes: Do not say the pressure at the top of a correct barometer column is large; the space there is empty and its pressure is almost zero.
Do not confuse the height of the mercury column with the length of the tube; the measured height is the vertical column height.
In P = ρgh, use the density of the liquid in the barometer. Water needs a much taller column than mercury because its density is lower.
When explaining a leak or trapped air, mention that air pressure above the mercury changes the column height and makes the reading incorrect.
